name: Highlands 1

nadir.desc: The nadir view shows a large single-story desert-style residence set well back from a paved road, accessed by a curved paved driveway that connects to the main road to the east|The property sits on a large parcel surrounded by open high-desert scrubland with scattered juniper trees|A rectangular in-ground pool is visible on the west side of the main structure, and a detached structure or wing is connected to the south side of the main building|The driveway terminates in a paved turnaround or motor court area adjacent to the northeast side of the residence.

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from the street side, revealing a long curved paved driveway that sweeps up from the road through open desert terrain to reach the residence|The driveway is wide enough for a single vehicle and traverses relatively flat to gently rolling terrain with scattered juniper trees on either side|The main structure is set back a significant distance from the road, with low-profile desert-style architecture visible at the end of the drive|No gates or barriers are visible along the driveway approach in this view.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the right side of the property, confirming the curved paved driveway entry from the lower right and its approach to the motor court area at the front-right of the residence|The main structure is multi-section with a flat roof, and the pool enclosure is visible to the left side of the structure|Scattered juniper trees are present between the driveway and the building, but none are directly obstructing the driveway path|The surrounding terrain on this side is open desert with no fencing visible.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, where a solar panel array is clearly visible on the roof of one section of the residence|The pool is visible in the foreground on this side, set within a defined patio area adjacent to the rear of the structure|A secondary unpaved track is visible along the far western edge of the parcel running roughly north-south, though it does not connect directly to the main structure|The rear of the property transitions directly into open desert scrubland with no fencing or walls observed.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property, with the pool and associated patio area visible on the right side of the frame adjacent to the main structure|The driveway entry and motor court are visible at the upper left of the frame, confirming the single paved access route|A faint unpaved track is visible along the lower portion of the property running east-west, separate from the main driveway|The left side of the residence has no visible secondary access doors or gates in this view.

considerations: The property is accessed by a single long curved paved driveway from the main road, requiring all responding units to enter and exit via the same route; the driveway width supports one vehicle at a time and the turnaround at the motor court allows apparatus repositioning. The residence is set a significant distance from the road, which will extend hose lay distances for fire suppression operations. The surrounding open desert scrubland with scattered juniper trees covers the entire parcel perimeter, and no perimeter fencing is visible, allowing foot access around all sides of the structure. A solar panel array is present on the roof, which is relevant for fire operations and responder safety on or near the roof.
clarifications: Is the driveway surface rated to support the weight of a fully loaded fire apparatus or heavy emergency vehicle? Are there any locked gates or access control devices at or near the driveway entrance from the main road? Does the unpaved track visible along the western and southern edges of the parcel provide a usable secondary access route to the rear of the structure? Are there propane tanks, fuel storage, or other above-ground utilities located on the property that are not visible from aerial imagery? Is the pool water accessible for emergency water supply operations?
